text: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market) Scheme Guidelines & Mandi Rules: 1. Purpose: e-NAM is a pan-India electronic trading portal that networks existing APMC mandis to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities. 2. Registration & Trading: Farmers can register free of charge at their local APMC e-NAM kiosk or online portal using their Aadhaar card and bank account details. 3. Quality Testing & Assaying: Mandis provide free automated quality testing and assaying labs to grade farmer produce before online bidding. 4. Direct Payment Transfer: Sale proceeds are directly transferred electronically into the farmer's linked bank account within 24 to 48 hours of trade settlement.

Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme Rules & Guidelines: 1. Eligibility: All farmers, individual/joint borrowers, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, and Self Help Groups (SHGs) are eligible for KCC. 2. Loan Limits & Interest Subvention: The government provides an interest subvention of 2% per annum for short-term crop loans up to Rs. 3 Lakhs. An additional 3% prompt repayment incentive (PRI) is given to farmers who pay on time, reducing the effective interest rate to 4% per annum. 3. Collateral Waiver: Collateral security is waived for KCC agricultural credit loans up to Rs. 1.60 Lakhs (extended up to Rs. 2.00 Lakhs for tie-up loans). 4. Validity & Processing Fee: The KCC card is valid for 5 years with annual review. Processing fees are waived for KCC loans up to Rs. 3 Lakhs.

PACS (Primary Agricultural Credit Societies) Model Bylaws: 1. Membership Criteria: Any farmer, rural artisan, or laborer residing within the operational area of the PACS is eligible for A-class membership with voting rights upon purchasing a minimum of 1 share. 2. Crop Loan Disbursement: Scale of Finance (SoF) determined by District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) governs maximum short-term credit allowed per acre for specified crops. 3. Non-Agricultural Credit: PACS can provide short-term credit for allied activities like dairy, poultry, fisheries, and micro-enterprises up to 20% of total loan portfolio.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) Rules: 1. Premium Rates: Uniform maximum premium payable by farmers is 2% for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for Annual Commercial/Horticultural crops. 2. Loss Assessment Window: Post-harvest losses covered up to a maximum period of 14 days for crops kept in cut and spread condition in the field against unseasonal cyclonic rains. 3. Intimation Period: Individual localized calamities (landslide, hailstorm, inundation) must be reported by the farmer within 72 hours of the loss event via the Crop Insurance App or local PACS kiosk.

Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme Operational Guidelines: 1. Purpose: Provides status of soil nutrient status and recommendations on appropriate dosage of nutrients/fertilizers for improving soil health and crop yields. 2. Sampling Cycle: Soil samples are collected once every 2 years in grid formats (2.5 ha for irrigated land, 10 ha for rainfed land) by local agriculture departments. 3. Recommended Parameters: Tests 12 parameters including N, P, K (Macro-nutrients), S (Secondary nutrient), Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, Bo (Micro-nutrients), and pH, EC, OC (Physical parameters). 4. Subsidies: Farmers receive soil testing and card generation completely free of charge funded under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA).
